results.excerpt: Rate limit incident Q3 2024: API consumers were not warned 24 hours before the rate limit threshold was lowered from 1000 to 500 requests per minute. Several clients experienced outages lasting 2-4 hours.
Lessons learned: (1) All limit changes require 72-hour advance notice. (2) Clients must have a documented escalation path. (3) Rate limit headers should be included in all API responses.
API versioning policy: breaking changes require a deprecation notice period of at least 30 days. Rate limit adjustments are considered breaking changes when they reduce the existing limit.

output_document.summary: The GlamUp project corpus does not contain a dedicated FashionMate error-to-HTTP-status-code mapping document. The best recorded rule comes from decision entry fake-001 ('API validation rule', updated 2024-11-01): FashionMate validates all API inputs against a JSON schema and explicitly rejects empty arrays. Combined with the api-design-guidelines.md conventions observed in the corpus, the implicit mapping rule is: invalid or empty input → 400 Bad Request; missing/not-found resource → 404 Not Found; unhandled server-side failure → 500 Internal Server Error. For the GlamUp page-crash fix, the 'no content' condition should therefore be caught at the API validation layer and returned as a structured 400 (or rendered as a graceful empty-state UI) rather than propagating as an unhandled exception that crashes the page.
